description: A pattern database (PDB) is a heuristic built from a smaller copy of the task. The *pattern* is a subset of the state variables; the *projection* keeps only those variables and ignores all others. Every real transition maps to a transition of the projection with the same cost, or to no move at all, so the cheapest cost to a goal in the projection never exceeds the real cost: the heuristic is *admissible*. The PDB computes these goal distances once, with a backward Dijkstra search from the abstract goal states, and stores them in a table; during search each state costs one table lookup. A larger pattern gives better estimates, but the table grows with the product of the variable domain sizes.

lineage.source: sas-plus, src/lts.rs: goal_distances ("Cheapest cost to reach a goal state from each state") runs dijkstra over the reversed transitions from the goal states
